angle.text: Where is your main water shutoff? Find and record it

copy.text: Where is your main water shutoff? Find and record it

scenes.why: The hook is the guide's own title: the question it answers, as a person would put it.

copy.text: Check the inspection report, plumbing records, or building information for the supply entry point.
Ask the landlord, building manager, utility, or plumber which valve serves your unit or house.
Follow accessible visible pipework only where it is safe to do so.
Confirm whether domestic water and fire sprinklers have separate branches.

eyebrow.text: Find and document the correct valve

scenes.why: The guide's own checklist, the first sentence of each item, ticked in as it is read.

caption.text: Care and seasonal work raised when it is due, never a permanent list

scenes.why: The turn: the product the guide itself hands over to, named and shown on its real screen, captioned with its listing's line closest to what the guide teaches. Screen: "A couple of things need a look" (Your home now: what's wrong, what to care for, what's coming up and what's handled, with the fridge and a dripping tap flagged.) chosen because it is the real screen closest to "Care and seasonal work raised when it is due, never a permanent list Where is yo"; focus on "Wrong, To care for, Coming up, Handled".
Ends on where to read the whole guide, with the product beneath it: the viewer leaves with the next step, not only a pitch.

reasoning.decision: YouTube Short, 1080×1920, 18–45s, hook by 1.2s, sound on

reasoning.decision: You own or rent a home and would rather be told what needs you this week than keep a mental list you know is incomplete. / You want the boring, expensive things caught early: the water heater, the gutters, the outside tap before the first freeze.
reasoning.because: The listing's own audience lines; the director writes for them.

reasoning.because: Every structure Home Base's copy supports at YouTube Short's normal line length is already used by its other films; a longer real line beats telling the same story twice.

reasoning.decision: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "tag"
reasoning.because: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "tag": things in the home are tagged, so scenes rise like a tag being lifted.
Camera "dolly": constant forward movement for a high-energy feed.
Grounds ink → light → light → accent: a cool accent, so a darker ground is used for contrast at a turn.
Its shape was 0.90 similar to guide-fall-home-maintenance-checklist--youtube-short; a different film, not the same one re-coloured.
Sound-on placement: every transition, landing and reveal has a cue, and the bed ducks under the brand moment.
Each scene is held for the time its words take to read on YouTube Short (0.26s a word), inside 18–45s.
